title: Add Ctrl+Shift+C/V to existing Foot clipboard bindings
head: 25fd779306fa
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: An existing symlinked Foot config is silently replaced by a new regular file
leads.consequence: With ~/.config/foot/foot.ini symlinked to a dotfile containing the legacy assignments, sed -i replaces the link instead of updating its target. The visible path is now repaired, but the user's managed dotfile still has the legacy shortcuts; later dotfile updates no longer reach Foot through that link. Both sed commands exit zero and omarchy-migrate records a completion marker, so reruns will not reconnect it. The other open repair, #13446, explicitly preserves symlinks but runs after this timestamp, too late to restore a link already severed.

leads.summary: Open PR #7309's repository-wide symlink-safety test fails on this migration
leads.consequence: #7309 (open, non-stacked, GitHub reports MERGEABLE on its own) adds a test that scans every migrations/ file for bare sed -i calls and fails unless the file is allowlisted or uses --follow-symlinks. This PR adds exactly two violations. Both distinct migrations and tests can coexist, but once #7309 also lands the combined tree's shell suite will fail on these two new lines. Adding --follow-symlinks resolves both the test failure and B1; do not allowlist this user-config rewrite.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator (PR #7309 diff adds sed-follow-symlinks-test.sh; Sol sealed run output lists 1790476654.sh:14 and :18) and by Opus plan-5 run

leads.summary: Duplicate guard misses equivalent Foot modifier order and introduces an invalid collision
leads.consequence: A valid [key-bindings] search-start=Shift+Control+c next to legacy clipboard-copy=Control+Insert is not matched by the literal Control+Shift+c grep. The migration adds Control+Shift+c to copy, even though Foot sorts the modifier names before collision comparison. foot --check-config rejects the result. Normal Foot launch drops the later of the two conflicting bindings (which one depends on file order), leaving either the user's search shortcut or Super+C broken. The migration itself exits zero and is marked complete.

leads.summary: Whole-file, case-insensitive grep mistakes comments and other modes for an active terminal chord
leads.consequence: A comment '# Old note: search-start=Control+Shift+c' suppresses copy repair, and a [search-bindings] clipboard-paste=Control+Shift+v suppresses normal paste repair despite binding a different mode. An uppercase Control+Shift+C also suppresses copy repair even though Foot documents that Shift+uppercase C never triggers. All scenarios retain a legacy key-bindings assignment, return zero, and get a completed migration marker; Super+C or Super+V remains broken until manual repair.

leads.summary: Partial existing binding suppresses the missing terminal chord
leads.consequence: If a legacy copy line already has XF86Copy but not Control+Shift+c, the OR-ed grep sees XF86Copy and skips the entire copy repair. The reverse situation (Control+Shift+c already present but XF86Copy absent) likewise skips the remaining packaged key, and the same holds for paste. The migration reports success and marks itself complete though Super+C still cannot copy in the first case. Add only each missing chord to the exact legacy line while checking collisions independently.
leads.triage: dropped: Control+Insert XF86Copy is a customized line the exact-match sed never touches regardless of the guard; by design

leads.summary: Migration hardcodes ~/.config but Foot honors XDG_CONFIG_HOME
leads.consequence: When a user relocates Foot configuration under XDG_CONFIG_HOME, Foot reads that config, but this migration checks only $HOME/.config/foot/foot.ini. With only the relocated legacy file present it exits zero, leaving the active config broken; omarchy-migrate then permanently marks the repair done. A stale file at ~/.config is changed instead if present.
leads.triage: dropped: XDG_CONFIG_HOME; repo migrations use $HOME/.config by convention (1 of 36 honours XDG)

leads.summary: Unscoped sed changes explicitly customized bindings in Foot search mode
leads.consequence: With both legacy [key-bindings] entries and an explicit [search-bindings] clipboard-paste=Shift+Insert, sed -i rewrites both occurrences and adds Control+Shift+v XF86Paste in search mode as well. This overrides the user's search-mode mapping although only normal terminal bindings need repair. The migration exits zero, marker is written, and subsequent runs do not revert the change. Scope replacement to [key-bindings] only.
leads.triage: dropped: search-bindings clipboard-paste rewrite; minor edge case needing a customized search section

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The migration replaces a symlinked `~/.config/foot/foot.ini` with a regular file, including configs it does not change.

### `sed -i` breaks dotfile symlinks

`migrations/1790476654.sh` lines 14 and 18 use plain `sed -i`, which renames a temporary file over the path. The `grep` guards only check that the chords are absent, so `sed` also runs on configs with no legacy line. **Impact:** a `foot.ini` that is itself a symlink into a dotfiles repo becomes a regular copy on update unless it already has both chords (a symlinked `~/.config/foot` directory is not affected). For a legacy config, the dotfile keeps the Insert-only lines.

**Suggested change:** use `sed -i --follow-symlinks` in both calls, as `migrations/1788745941.sh` does, and add a symlink case to the test.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 25fd779)</summary>

# Reproducer: the migration replaces a symlinked foot.ini with a regular file

Reviewed head: `25fd779306fa70e38dbeb8d0b3f43d8d797ecc77` (PR #13378).
Environment of the recorded run: GNU bash 5.3.15, GNU sed 4.10, isolated sandbox with a temporary `HOME`.

Save as `test/shell.d/foot-clipboard-symlink-test.sh` next to the PR's own test and run `bash test/shell.d/foot-clipboard-symlink-test.sh` from the repository root.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

# Dotfile setups symlink ~/.config/foot/foot.ini. The migration has to leave
# the link in place: untouched when there is nothing to change, and written
# through when the legacy lines are there.

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

migration="$ROOT/migrations/1790476654.sh"
test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

foot_config="$test_tmp/home/.config/foot/foot.ini"
dotfile="$test_tmp/dotfiles/foot.ini"

run_migration() {
  HOME="$test_tmp/home" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" bash -euo pipefail "$migration" >/dev/null
}

link_dotfile() {
  rm -rf "$test_tmp/home" "$test_tmp/dotfiles"
  mkdir -p "${foot_config%/*}" "${dotfile%/*}"
  printf '%s\n' "$@" >"$dotfile"
  ln -s "$dotfile" "$foot_config"
}

# A config that relies on Foot's default clipboard bindings needs nothing.
link_dotfile "[main]" "font=Iosevka:size=11"
run_migration || fail "migration exits clean on a symlinked config without clipboard bindings"
[[ -L $foot_config ]] ||
  fail "a symlinked config the migration does not change stays a symlink" "foot.ini is now a $(stat -c %F "$foot_config")"
pass "migration leaves a symlinked config it does not change alone"

link_dotfile "[key-bindings]" "clipboard-copy=Control+Insert" "primary-paste=none" "clipboard-paste=Shift+Insert"
run_migration || fail "migration exits clean on a symlinked legacy config"
[[ -L $foot_config ]] || fail "a symlinked legacy config stays a symlink" "foot.ini is now a $(stat -c %F "$foot_config")"
grep -qx "clipboard-copy=Control+Insert Control+Shift+c XF86Copy" "$dotfile" ||
  fail "the symlink target gets the chords" "$(cat "$dotfile")"
pass "migration writes through a symlinked legacy config"
```

Actual output at the reviewed head (exit 1):

```text
foot.ini is now a regular file
not ok - a symlinked config the migration does not change stays a symlink
```

Actual output with only `--follow-symlinks` added to the two `sed -i` calls in `migrations/1790476654.sh` (exit 0):

```text
ok - migration leaves a symlinked config it does not change alone
ok - migration writes through a symlinked legacy config
```

The PR's own `foot-clipboard-bindings-migration-test.sh` still passes (5 of 5) with that change.

Change used for the second run:

```diff
 if ! grep -qiE '(^|[[:space:]=])(Control\+Shift\+c|XF86Copy)([[:space:]]|$)' "$foot_config"; then
-  sed -i 's/^clipboard-copy=Control+Insert[[:space:]]*$/clipboard-copy=Control+Insert Control+Shift+c XF86Copy/' "$foot_config"
+  sed -i --follow-symlinks 's/^clipboard-copy=Control+Insert[[:space:]]*$/clipboard-copy=Control+Insert Control+Shift+c XF86Copy/' "$foot_config"
 fi
 
 if ! grep -qiE '(^|[[:space:]=])(Control\+Shift\+v|XF86Paste)([[:space:]]|$)' "$foot_config"; then
-  sed -i 's/^clipboard-paste=Shift+Insert[[:space:]]*$/clipboard-paste=Shift+Insert Control+Shift+v XF86Paste/' "$foot_config"
+  sed -i --follow-symlinks 's/^clipboard-paste=Shift+Insert[[:space:]]*$/clipboard-paste=Shift+Insert Control+Shift+v XF86Paste/' "$foot_config"
 fi
```

Why: GNU `sed -i` writes a new file and renames it over the path, which replaces a symlink with a regular file unless `--follow-symlinks` is given. The `grep` guards only check that the chords are absent, so `sed -i` also runs on configs where no line matches, such as a config with no `[key-bindings]` at all.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Open PR #7309 adds `test/shell.d/sed-follow-symlinks-test.sh`, which rejects bare `sed -i` under `migrations/`. Run against this migration, it reports `migrations/1790476654.sh:14` and `:18`. The suggested change resolves both.
- **Verified:** Foot 1.28.0 `--check-config` accepts the result for the stock 3.8.0–3.8.2 and 3.8.3–3.8.4 files, with and without later quattro migrations, and the 3.8.3–3.8.4 file with a changed font; the `[key-bindings]` section then equals the packaged one.
- **Verified:** a second run changes nothing; a missing config is left alone; a 0600 file stays 0600.
- **Verified:** the PR's test passes at head and merged onto `quattro` at b421b1b, and fails against a no-op migration and against one with the chord guards removed.
- **Optional test improvement:** `stat -c %a == 644` depends on the checkout's umask (a checkout under `umask 002` gives the file mode 664, so the check would fail there); `[[ ! -x $migration ]]` checks the part Git controls, that the file is not executable.
</details>

<details><summary>More findings: the chord guard is a text match</summary>

The guard matches the literal text `Control+Shift+c` case-insensitively anywhere in the file, while Foot sorts modifiers, treats key names case-sensitively and keeps search and normal bindings apart. A legacy config with `search-start=Shift+Control+c` still gets `Control+Shift+c` added, which `foot --check-config` rejects with exit 230. The same happens when the colliding binding is in an `include=` file. Conversely, a comment mentioning the chord, an uppercase `Control+Shift+C`, `XF86Copy` bound elsewhere (where `Control+Shift+c` alone was safe to add), or `Control+Shift+v` in `[search-bindings]` makes it skip a fix that was safe. Each case needs a customized config that still has an untouched legacy line; no config Omarchy shipped triggers them.

**Suggested change:** judge each chord separately and compare only active `[key-bindings]`/`[text-bindings]` entries, with modifiers sorted and the key matched case-sensitively; a collision in an `include=` file still needs `foot --check-config`, so note that gap in the PR.

# Reproducer: a chord bound with the modifiers in another order is mapped twice

Reviewed head: `25fd779306fa70e38dbeb8d0b3f43d8d797ecc77` (PR #13378).
Environment of the recorded run: GNU bash 5.3.15, GNU sed 4.10, Foot 1.28.0 (`foot --check-config`), isolated sandbox with a temporary `HOME`.

Foot 1.28.0 parses a combo's modifiers into a list and sorts it (`parse_modifiers()` in `config.c`), then compares sorted lists (`modifiers_equal()`), so `Shift+Control+c` and `Control+Shift+c` are the same binding. The migration's guard only matches the literal text `Control+Shift+c`.

Save as `test/shell.d/foot-clipboard-collision-test.sh` next to the PR's own test and run `bash test/shell.d/foot-clipboard-collision-test.sh` from the repository root (it skips the Foot check when Foot is not installed).

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

# Foot sorts modifiers before comparing bindings, so Shift+Control+c is the
# same combination as Control+Shift+c. A legacy config that binds it to another
# action must not get a second mapping.

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

migration="$ROOT/migrations/1790476654.sh"
test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

foot_config="$test_tmp/home/.config/foot/foot.ini"

run_migration() {
  HOME="$test_tmp/home" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" bash -euo pipefail "$migration" >/dev/null
}

mkdir -p "${foot_config%/*}"
printf '%s\n' "[key-bindings]" "clipboard-copy=Control+Insert" "primary-paste=none" "clipboard-paste=Shift+Insert" \
  "search-start=Shift+Control+c" >"$foot_config"
run_migration || fail "migration exits clean when a reordered chord is taken"
cat "$foot_config"

if command -v foot >/dev/null; then
  check_exit=0
  check_output=$(HOME="$test_tmp/home" foot --check-config --config="$foot_config" 2>&1) || check_exit=$?
  printf '%s\n' "${check_output//$test_tmp/\$TMP}"
  (( check_exit == 0 )) || fail "foot accepts the migrated config" "foot --check-config exited $check_exit"
  pass "foot accepts the migrated config"
else
  skip "Foot not installed; skipping foot --check-config"
fi
```

Actual output at the reviewed head (exit 1; stdout then stderr):

```text
[key-bindings]
clipboard-copy=Control+Insert Control+Shift+c XF86Copy
primary-paste=none
clipboard-paste=Shift+Insert Control+Shift+v XF86Paste
search-start=Shift+Control+c
 err: config.c:2643: $TMP/home/.config/foot/foot.ini:5: [key-bindings].search-start: Control+Shift+c already mapped to 'clipboard-copy'
foot --check-config exited 230
not ok - foot accepts the migrated config
```

Before the migration the same file passes `foot --check-config` (exit 0). The same result (exit 230) was recorded when the colliding `search-start=Control+Shift+c` lives in a file pulled in with `include=` rather than in `foot.ini` itself.

At normal startup Foot does not refuse the file: `config_override_apply()` returns the collision result, and `config_load()` only fails on it when errors are fatal (`--check-config`). Foot starts, shows the error, and drops the later of the two bindings (`resolve_key_binding_collisions()` removes the more recent entry), which here is the user's `search-start`.
</details>

<details><summary>Other open PRs for this issue</summary>

- #13446: rewrites only exact legacy lines inside `[key-bindings]`, judges each chord separately and writes through symlinks; misses `[text-bindings]` collisions and legacy lines with CRLF or trailing whitespace.
- #13649: appends `Control+Shift+c`/`v` (no XF86 keys) to any `clipboard-copy=`/`clipboard-paste=` line, including customized ones, with no collision check; also carries unrelated `windows-vm` changes.

The three use different migration filenames, so there is no file conflict, but all three would run in timestamp order and can compound in edge cases.
</details>
